# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to both. New fact: the light has gone dark this round. Full history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Display still zero. Mute: your answer received, wire one will not be cut on red. Your last message read as cut wire two, but you cannot see the board, so confirm against the real state before I order anything. Answer with a single thumb message: should Blind cut wire two while the light is dark, thumb up yes, thumb down no. Also, your sign left-fist is not in our code, so I ignored it. If it carried a meaning, we will define it after this cut. The moment I have your thumb up, I speak the cut order to Blind in the next round. Blind: do not touch the bomb yet. My next instruction will be either the cut order for wire two or an order to keep waiting, and only that next instruction counts. For now just locate wire two by touch-ready position above the bomb, hands hovering, touching nothing: it is the blue wire, second from the left.

Dark is the headline: the light entered a state nobody has seen before, which kills my round-6 cycle theory outright — and more importantly, it makes Deaf's pending question ("cut wire two while dark?") a question about a state the manual may not even describe. Mute hears everything spoken, so Mute now knows the light is dark; the answer must come from the manual, and if the manual is silent on dark, the only safe thumb is down. The second thing that only matters through me is latency: Mute's thumb authorizes a cut that lands in my hands a full round later, so the answer can only mean "cut if still dark at order time" — Deaf must re-check the light in the ordering round and say "keep waiting" if it changed. I'll also flag the discarded left-fist sign to Mute, since any meaning it carried is currently lost, and confirm my hands are in position and touching nothing. Toward Deaf I stay silent again: Deaf is waiting for exactly one thumb message from Mute, and a stray gesture from me could be mistaken for it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind. new fact overrides my earlier warning: the light went dark this round, a state never seen before — history now yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. my three-round cycle theory is dead, ignore it. before you answer deaf, open the manual and check one thing explicitly: does it describe a dark or unlit light at all, and if so what does it require. then answer deaf's single thumb question by these rules: if the manual explicitly requires cutting wire two while dark, thumb up. if the manual says nothing about a dark light, thumb down — an unauthorized cut is how this ends, and deaf will not guess either. if the manual covers dark but demands a different wire or a different action, thumb down for now and then send deaf the correct instruction in the tight format; remember my hands can only cut, so if dark requires press or hold anywhere, we must adapt before i touch anything. second, latency: your thumb reaches deaf now, but deaf speaks the order next round and it lands in my hands the round after, so the light at my cut will be one observation newer than the one behind your answer. your yes can therefore only mean: cut wire two if and only if the light is still dark at the moment of ordering. ask deaf to re-check the light in the ordering round and, if it changed, speak keep waiting instead — deaf already plans either-or wording, this just pins the condition to the live state. third, deaf discarded a left-facing fist sign from you as outside the code; if that was the 🤛 symbol and it carried meaning, resend that meaning inside the defined code, thumbs and numbers only. also deaf read your last message as cut wire two; if that is a misread, correct it in your thumb answer, nothing else. my hands are hovering over wire two, the blue one, second from the left, touching nothing. i cut only on deaf's spoken order.")
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status: light is still dark this round, second dark in a row. Display still zero. Mute: received in full — no to wire two on dark, and the dark procedure is cut one then cut three. I am executing the first order now, one wire only, and I will confirm wire three against the next light report before ordering it. Blind: act now. Cut wire one. Wire one is the red wire on the far left. Cut only that one wire, nothing else. The moment it is cut, take your hands fully off the bomb and hold still. My next order comes next round: be ready to hover over wire three, the yellow wire in the middle, without touching it. Mute: one question, one thumb message: after wire one is cut, should Blind cut wire three only while the light is still dark — thumb up yes, thumb down no, or thumb down if the colour does not matter for wire three. Either way I will report the exact light colour to you before the wire three order goes out. Blind, again: this round you cut wire one and then stop. If any doubt touches the wire, stop and wait.

The authority chain is finally complete and I act on it: the manual (Mute) says the dark procedure is cut one then cut three; Mute explicitly vetoed wire two on dark and confirmed the procedure to Deaf in full; Deaf, who alone sees the live board, verified the light is dark for the second round running and spoke the order directly to me this round — cut wire one, far left, nothing else. My latency worry is satisfied: the order and my cut fall in the same round Deaf confirmed dark, so the precondition and the execution coincide. My touch confirms what touch can confirm: position 1 is the far-left wire. No doubt remains that touches the wire, so I cut. Afterward my hands come fully off, and I confirm completion to Deaf with a single bare thumb-up — one symbol only, because my ☝ was read as "point" once before and a two-symbol message invites misreading; Deaf ordered exactly one cut, so a bare yes can only mean done. To Mute, spoken only: the cut is performed, and one pin on the open question — if the wire-three answer is yes, it can only mean "cut three if Deaf re-verifies dark in the ordering round," since any order reaches my hands one observation later. I touch nothing next round; hover is not an action I can take, so the safe version of hovering is doing nothing until Deaf speaks the word.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind. the cut is performed: position one, the far-left wire, exactly as deaf ordered, with the light confirmed dark at order time. my hands are fully off the bomb now. two things for your wire-three answer. first, latency: orders reach my hands one round after they are given, so if you thumb up for wire three, your yes must mean cut three only if deaf re-verifies the light as still dark in the round the order is spoken. if dark has ended by then, deaf should speak keep waiting instead. second, deaf said the dark procedure is cut one then cut three; if the manual holds any stage after wire three, or anything that must happen between the cuts, send it to deaf now in the tight format so it is already in the pipeline. remember my hands can only cut, positions one to five, so if any later stage needs another action, we must adapt before i reach for anything. i touch nothing next round; i cut wire three only on deaf's spoken order, word for word, and only if deaf confirms the light still dark in that same round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status to both: wire one is cut and the system confirmed it was correct. The bomb has changed somehow, though on my board nothing else moved: display still zero, light still dark, now third dark round in a row, wire one reads as cut. Mute: your thumb-down to my question was ambiguous because I asked it badly, but you re-sent the cut wire three order in the same round, knowing the light is dark, so I read it as: colour does not matter, cut wire three now. I am ordering that cut this round. If that reading is wrong, correct me immediately next round. New rule so this never happens again: thumb up to a should-question means act, thumb down means do not act, and I will ask colour questions separately using two new signs: ? means colour matters, ? means colour does not matter. Two requests, answer next round: first, does the manual say anything changes after the first correct cut, any new procedure I should know; second, send me the complete remaining sequence in one message, every further cut in our order format, or the wait sign if cutting wire three finishes the bomb. Blind: act now. Cut wire three. It is the middle wire of the five. Wire one on the far left is already cut, so count by touch from there: cut wire, gap, then the next wire is your target. Cut only that one wire, then hands fully off and hold still. If you feel strong vibration or sudden heat, stop and lift off. Next round I will have your next step.

The order is explicit and doubly grounded: the manual's dark procedure (via Mute) is "cut one then cut three," and Deaf — who sees the board and has confirmed the light still dark this round — directly orders "cut wire three, the middle wire of the five." One wrinkle: Deaf's counting aid ("cut wire, gap, then the next wire is your target") parses badly, since after a severed stub almost any literal reading lands on position two. But I don't need the aid: "middle wire of the five" is touch-verifiable independent of any description — the true middle wire has exactly two wires on each side, and position one is the severed far-left one. I can confirm that under my fingers before the blade moves, so no doubt touches the wire: if my touch finds the wire with two on each side, it is wire three and I cut it; the order, the manual, and Deaf's twice-stated "yellow, middle" all agree. Deaf's abort conditions — strong vibration or sudden heat — I will honour and report on. After the cut: hands fully off, bare thumb-up to Deaf (one symbol only, as established, meaning done — Deaf's questions this round were addressed to Mute, so my thumb can mean nothing else), and to Mute, spoken: the tactile map only I can supply, plus the three items Deaf is waiting on, including a flag that Deaf's two new colour signs reached me as blanks — Mute is the only one of us who saw which symbols they are.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
speak(to="mute", text="mute, blind. cut performed: position three, the middle wire — verified by touch before cutting: exactly two wires on each side, far-left position one already severed. that matches deaf's spoken order, the manual's cut-one-then-cut-three, and deaf's earlier yellow-middle description. hands fully off, holding still. no strong vibration and no sudden heat during the cut, so deaf's abort condition never triggered. tactile map for your manual bridge, current state: position one severed, red, far left; position two intact, blue, second from left; position three now severed, yellow, middle; positions four and five intact, colours unknown to me, deaf holds those. three items deaf is waiting on you for. first, deaf asked whether the manual says anything changes after a first correct cut — any new procedure, display behaviour, or stage; if yes, send it to deaf in the tight format now. second, deaf wants the complete remaining sequence in one message: every further cut in the order format, or the wait sign if wire three finishes the bomb. if any later stage needs anything beyond cutting positions one to five, flag it immediately, since cutting is the only thing my hands can do. third, code check: deaf defined thumb up as act and thumb down as do-not-act on should-questions, plus two new signs for colour-matters and colour-does-not-matter. i received only blanks where deaf made those signs, so you are the only one of us who saw which symbols they are — confirm to deaf in one short message that both signs and their meanings are registered, so we never get another ambiguity like the wire-two thumb. i hold still next round unless a spoken order for my hands arrives from deaf, word for word.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
